claims.quote: White has a rook and four pawns (g2, g4, h3, and the rook on a4)
claims.why: White has only three pawns (g2, g4, h3); the rook on a4 is not a pawn.

claims.quote: two rooks and a bishop against White's lone king and pawns
claims.why: After 56. Rxe1 White still has its rook on e1, which is never captured in the line.

claims.quote: White has a rook, bishop, knight and five pawns
claims.why: White has four pawns (a3, f3, g3, h4).

claims.quote: White trades bishops
claims.why: In the Rb3 line White's bishop takes Black's bishop on c7 and is never captured (it goes on to take on a5), so no bishops are traded.

claims.quote: since Black gets ...f5 in with tempo
claims.why: After 20. O-O f5 the f5 pawn attacks nothing (e4 and g4 are empty) and uncovers no attack, so the move carries no threat that gains a tempo; White answers with the quiet 21. Rfe1.

claims.quote: Bf3 adds protection to d4
claims.why: The bishop is light-squared and d4 is a dark square; a bishop on f3 does not defend d4.

claims.quote: White's queen on g4 is attacked by Black's bishop on g5
claims.why: The bishop on g5 stands on the same file as the queen and only attacks f4, h4, f6 and h6; nothing attacks g4 (the d4 queen is blocked by the f4 pawn).

claims.quote: The engine line is 15. h3 Rfc8 16. Rfc1 Rb4 17. Bh4 Nb6
claims.why: No engine line contains h3 Rfc8 Rfc1 Rb4 Bh4 Nb6; the h3 line continues 17. Bh4 Rcb8 (Bh4 Nb6 belongs to the Rfc1 line), even though the answer then corrects itself.

claims.quote: queenside pawn majority to push
claims.why: White has a4, b4 against Black's a7, b7, c6 on the queenside (3 v 3 even counting d4), so White has no queenside majority.

claims.quote: It is supported by the rook on b1
claims.why: The rook on b1 does not defend c2; it attacks along the first rank and the b-file only, and nothing defends the c2 pawn.

claims.quote: It is only a slight edge by comparison.
claims.why: Rgf1 is rated 103cp, which the prompt's scale puts in the 101-250 'Clear/Significant advantage' band, not a slight edge.

claims.quote: Both sides have their rooks on open or semi-open files.
claims.why: Black's rooks are on the d-file (blocked by Black's own d4 pawn) and the f-file (behind Black's own f7 pawn), so neither is on an open or semi-open file.

claims.quote: Black's bishop on b4 pins the knight on c3 against the pawn on e4 and the king's side of the board
claims.why: Behind c3 on the b4 diagonal is White's own d2 pawn, so the knight is not pinned to anything (and e4 is not on that line).

claims.quote: White's bishop pair
claims.why: White has only one bishop (c1) after 4. Bxc6; it is Black who has two bishops (f8, g4).

claims.quote: White also has the extra material
claims.why: Both sides have a rook and a knight, and Black has five pawns to White's four, so Black has the extra material before Rxd8+.

claims.quote: White's queen gets lost while Black picks up pawns
claims.why: The Bxb8 line ends with Qxc1+, a capture White recaptures (Rxc1), so the queens are traded, not White's queen lost.

claims.quote: White is up a knight and several pawns
claims.why: White has 5 pawns against Black's 4, so White is up a knight and one pawn, not several pawns.

claims.quote: But that pawn is loose
claims.why: The c4 pawn is defended by Black's b5 pawn, so Bxc4 or Nxc4 would just be met by bxc4.

claims.quote: Black has also traded off the dark-squared bishop
claims.why: Black did not trade it: after 7. Bxd6 Black played 7...dxc4 instead of recapturing, and White still has its dark-squared bishop on g3.

claims.quote: It keeps Black's king stuck in the center
claims.why: In the Qb5+ line Black castles at once with 18...O-O, as the answer itself notes.

claims.quote: the offside knight is rerouted to b3
claims.why: The a2 knight cannot reach b3; the 21. Nb3 in the O-O line is played by the knight from d4.

claims.quote: Material stays level through the line
claims.why: Black is already a pawn up (8 pawns to 7, pieces equal); the FACTS say material is unchanged over the line, not that it is level.

claims.quote: it also pins nothing now, since the knight on c6 is shielded by the d-pawn and queen setup
claims.why: d7 is empty, so the bishop on b5 pins the c6 knight to the king on e8 (which is why ...Nxd4 is illegal).

claims.quote: damages Black's pawn structure with doubled c-pawns
claims.why: Black's c-pawn already left with 3...cxd4, so after Bxc6+ bxc6 Black has a single c-pawn, not doubled c-pawns.
